notes: The verse is corrupt. 'hitājñayā śrīghṛṇino gurur vai lulokanyugāthaḥ samālikhadvai' probably stands for 'hitājñayā śrīghṛṇino guror vai lokanāthaḥ samālikhad vai': Lokanātha wrote it at the order of his guru, (Śrī) Ghṛṇin. The teacher's name is uncertain, since ghṛṇi- could also be a corrupt epithet. 'tyaktaś ca hyunānayugaiḥ' is unclear and may hide a further chronogram or the scribe's age. The scribe calls himself young and 16 years old (yunā … ṣoḍaśavarṣeṇa), 'kovidālpa', and born of a good lineage (ābrahmaparyanta sadvaṃśotpanna). The paksa is not stated. ŚS 1767 + 78 = c. 1845 CE (Vaiśākha falls in April–May 1845 if the year is expired). Caṃpākoṭa village lies north of Garuḍanārāyaṇa (Changu Narayan?) near the Bāgmatī. It is not securely identified, so it is left unnormalized.
